1.1: The word of the Lord that came to Joel the sonne of Pethuel.
1.2: Hear ye this, O Elders, and hearken ye all inhabitantes of the land, whether such a thing hath been in your dayes, or yet in the dayes of your fathers.
1.3: Tell you your children of it, and let your children shew to their children, and their children to another generation.
1.4: That which is left of ye palmer worm, hath the grashopper eaten, and the residue of ye grashopper hath the canker worm eaten, and the residue of the canker worm hath the caterpiller eaten.
1.5: Awake ye drunkards, and weep, and howl all ye drinkers of wine, because of the new wine: for it shalbe pulled from your mouth.
1.6: Yea, a nation cometh upon my land, mightie, and without nomber, whose teeth are like the teeth of a lyon, and he hath the iawes of a great lyon.
1.7: He maketh my vine waste, and pilleth off the bark of my figge tree: he maketh it bare, and casteth it down: ye branches therof are made white.
1.8: Mourn like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
1.9: The meat offring, and the drink offring is cut off from the House of the Lord: the Priests the Lords ministers mourn.
1.10: The field is wasted: the land mourneth: for the corn is destroyed: the new wine is dried up, and the oyle is decayed.
1.11: Be ye ashamed, O husband men: howl, O ye vine dressers for the wheat, and for the barly, because the harvest of the field is perished.
1.12: The vine is dried up, and the figge tree is decayed: the pomegranate tree and the palm tree, and the apple tree, even all the trees of the field are withered: surely the joy is withered away from the sonnes of men.
1.13: Gird your selves and lament, ye Priests: howl ye ministers of the altar: come, and lie all night in sackecloth, ye ministers of my God: for the meat offring, and the drink offring is taken away from the house of your God.
1.14: Sanctifie you a fast: call a solemn assemblie: gather the Elders, and all the inhabitants of the land into the House of the Lord your God, and cry unto the Lord,
1.15: Alas: for the day, for the day of the Lord is at hand, and it cometh as a destruction from the Almightie.
1.16: Is not the meat cut off before our eyes? and joy, and gladness from the house of our God?
1.17: The seed is rotten under their cloddes: the garners are destroyed: the barnes are broken down, for the corn is withered.
1.18: How did the beasts mourn! the herdes of cattel pine away, because they have no pasture, and the flockes of sheep are destroyed.
1.19: O Lord, to thee will I crie: for the fire hath deuoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burnt up all the trees of the field.
1.20: The beasts of the field cry also unto thee: for the rivers of waters are dried up, and the fire hath deuoured the pastures of the wildernes.

2.1: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and shout in mine holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the Lord is come: for it is at hand.
2.2: A day of darkenesse, and of blackness, a day of cloudes, and obscuritie, as the morning spred upon the mountaines, so is there a great people, and a mighty: there was none like it from the beginning, neither shalbe any more after it, unto the yeeres of many generations.
2.3: A fire deuoureth before him, and behind him a flame burneth up: the land is as the garden of Eden before him, and behind him a desolate wilderness, so that nothing shall escape him.
2.4: The beholding of him is like the sight of horses, and like the horsemen, so shall they runne.
2.5: Like the noyse of charrets in the toppes of the mountaines shall they leap, like the noyse of a flame of fire that deuoureth the stubble, and as a mightie people prepared to the battel.
2.6: Before his face shall the people tremble: all faces shall gather blackenesse.
2.7: They shall runne like strong men, and goe up to the wall like men of war, and every man shall goe forward in his wayes, and they shall not stay in their paths.
2.8: Neither shall one thrust another, but every one shall walk in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded.
2.9: They shall runne to and from in the citie: they shall runne upon the wall: they shall clime up upon the houses, and enter in at ye windowes like ye thief.
2.10: The earth shall tremble before him, ye heavens shall shake, the sunne and the moon shalbe dark, and the starres shall withdraw their shining,
2.11: And the Lord shall utter his voyce before his host: for his host is very great: for he is strog that doeth his word: for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible, and who can abide it?
2.12: Therefore also now the Lord sayth, Turn you unto me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning,
2.13: And rent your heart, and not your clothes: and turn unto the Lord your God, for he is gratious, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindnes, and repenteth him of the evil.
2.14: Who knoweth, is he wil return and repent and leave a blessing behind him, even a meat offring, and a drink offring unto ye Lord your God?
2.15: Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctifie a fast, call a solemn assembly.
2.16: Gather the people: sanctifie the congregation, gather the elders: assemble the children, and those that suck the breastes: let the bridegrome go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her bride chamber.
2.17: Let the Priestes, the ministers of the Lord weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage into reproche that the heathen should rule over them. Wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?
2.18: Then will the Lord be ielous over his land, and spare his people.
2.19: Yea, the Lord wil answer and say unto his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oyle, and you shalbe satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproche among the heathen,
2.20: But I will remooue far off from you the Northren armie, and I will drive him into a land, barren and desolate with his face toward the East sea, and his end to the utmost sea, and his stink shall come up, and his corruption shall ascend, because he hath exalted himself to do this.
2.21: Fear not, O land, but be glad, and reioyce: for the Lord wil do great things.
2.22: Be not afrayde, ye beastes of the field: for the pastures of the wilderness are green: for the tree beareth her fruit: the figge tree and the vine do give their force.
2.23: Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and reioyce in the Lord your God: for he hath given you the rayne of righteousnes, he wil cause to come down for you the rayne, even the first rain, and the latter rain in the first moneth.
2.24: And the barnes shalbe full of wheat, and the presses shall abound with wine and oyle.
2.25: And I will render you the yeeres that the grashopper hath eaten, the canker worm and the caterpiller and the palmer worm, my great host which I sent among you.
2.26: So you shall eat and be satisfied and praise the Name of the Lord your God, that hath dealt marueilously with you: and my people shall never be ashamed.
2.27: Ye shall also know, that I am in the middes of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God and none other, and my people shall never be ashamed.
2.28: And afterward will I powre out my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sonnes and your daughters shall prophecie: your old men shall dream dreames, and your yong men shall see visions,
2.29: And also upon the servants, and upon the maydes in those dayes wil I powre my Spirit.
2.30: And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth: blood and fire, and pillars of smoke.
2.31: The sunne shalbe turned into darkenesse, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come.
2.32: But whosoever shall call on the Name of the Lord, shalbe saved: for in mount Zion, and in Ierusale shalbe deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant, whom the Lord shall call.

3.1: For behold, in those dayes and in that time, when I shall bring again the captiuitie of Judah and Jerusalem,
3.2: I will also gather all nations, and wil bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people, and for mine heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.
3.3: And they have cast lottes for my people, and have given the child for the harlot, and sold the girl for wine, that they might drink.
3.4: Yea, and what have you to do with me, O Tyrus and Zidon and all the costes of Palestina? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompence mee, swiftly and speedily will I render your recompence upon your head:
3.5: For ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have caried into your temples my goodly and pleasant things.
3.6: The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have you sold unto the Grecians, that ye might send them far from their border.
3.7: Behold, I will rayse them out of the place where ye have sold them, and will render your reward upon your own head,
3.8: And I will send your sonnes and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off: for the Lord hath spoken it.
3.9: Publish this among the Gentiles: prepare war, wake up the mightie men: let all the men of war draw neere and come up.
3.10: Break your plowshares into swords, and your sithes into speares: let the weak say, I am strong.
3.11: Assemble your selves, and come all yee heathen and gather your selves together round about: there shall the Lord cast down the mightie men.
3.12: Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.
3.13: Put in your sithes, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down, for the winepress is full: yea, the winepresses runne over, for their wickedness is great.
3.14: O multitude, O multitude, come into the valley of threshing: for the day of the Lord is neere in the valley of threshing.
3.15: The sunne and moon shalbe darkened, and the starres shall withdraw their light.
3.16: The Lord also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voyce from Jerusalem, and the heavens and the earth shall shake, but the Lord wil be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel.
3.17: So shall ye know that I am the Lord your God dwelling in Zion, mine holy Mountain: then shall Jerusalem bee holy, and there shall no strangers go thorowe her any more.
3.18: And in that day shall the mountaines drop down new wine, and the hilles shall flow with milk, and al the rivers of Judah shall runne with waters, and a fountain shall come forth of the House of the Lord, and shall water the valley of Shittim.
3.19: Egypt shalbe waste, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the iniuries of the childre of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.
3.20: But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
3.21: For I will clense their blood, that I have not clensed, and the Lord will dwell in Zion.

29:1:2: He calleth the Jews to the consideration of God’s judgments, who had now plagued the fruits of the ground for the space of four years, which was for their sins, and to call them to repentance.
Signifying the Princes, the Priests and the governors.
29:1:5: Meaning, that the occasion of their excess and drunkenness was taken away.
29:1:6: This was another plague wherewith God had punished them when he stirred up the Assyrians against them.
29:1:8: Mourn grievously, as a woman which hath lost her husband to whom she hath been married in her youth.
29:1:9: The tokens of God’s wrath did appear in his Temple, insomuch as God’s service was left off.
29:1:10: All comfort and substance for nourishment is taken away.
29:1:13: He showeth that the only means to avoid God’s wrath, and to have all things restored, is unfeigned repentance.
29:1:15: We see by these great plagues that utter destruction is at hand.
29:2:1: He showeth the great judgments of God, which are at hand, except they repent.
29:2:3: The enemy destroyed our plentiful country, wheresoever he cometh.
29:2:6: They shall be pale and black for fear, as Nah. 2:10.
29:2:8: For none shall be able to resist them.
29:2:10: Read Joel 2:31 and Isa. 13:10; Ezek. 32:7; Joel 3:15; Matt. 24:29.
29:2:11: The Lord shall stir up the Assyrians to execute his judgments.
29:2:13: Mortify your affections and serve God with pureness of heart, and not with ceremonies.
29:2:14: He speaketh this to stir up their slothfulness, and not that he doubted of God’s mercies, if they did repent. How God repenteth, read Jer. 18:8.
29:2:16: That as all have sinned, so all may show forth signs of their repentance, that men seeing the children which are not free from God’s wrath, might be the more lively touched with the consideration of their own sins.
29:2:18: If they repent he showeth that God will preserve and defend them with a most ardent affection.
29:2:20: That is, the Assyrians your enemies.
Called the salt sea, or Persian sea: meaning, that though his army were so great that it filled all from this sea to the sea called Mediterranean, yet he would scatter them.
29:2:23: That is, such as should come by just measure, and as was wont to be sent when God was reconciled with them.
29:2:28: As they had visions and dreams in old time, so shall they now have clearer revelations.

That is, in greater abundance, and more generally than in times past: and this was fulfilled under Christ, when as God’s graces, and his Spirit under the Gospel was abundantly given to the Church, Isa. 44:3; Acts 2:17; John 7:38, 39.
29:2:30: He warneth the faithful what terrible things should come, to the intent that they should not look for continual quietness in this world, and yet in all these troubles he would preserve them.
29:2:31: The order of nature shall seem to be changed for the horrible afflictions that shall be in the world, Isa. 13:10; Ezek. 32:7; Joel 3:15; Matt. 24:29.
29:2:32: God’s judgments are for the destruction of the infidels, and to move the godly to call upon the Name of God, who will give them salvation.
29:3:1: When I shall deliver my Church, which standeth of the Jews and of the Gentiles.
29:3:2: It appeareth that he alludeth to that great victory of Jehoshaphat, when as God without man’s help destroyed the enemies, 2 Chron. 20:26, also he hath respect to this word Jehoshaphat which signifieth pleading or judgment, because God would judge the enemies of his Church, as he did there.
29:3:3: That which the enemy gat for the sale of my people, he bestowed upon harlots and drink.
29:3:4: He taketh the cause of his Church in hand against the enemy, as though the injury were done to himself.
Have I done you wrong, that ye will render me the like?
29:3:8: For afterward God sold them by Nebuchadnezzar and Alexander the great, for the love he bare to his people, and thereby they were comforted, as though the price had been theirs.
29:3:10: When I shall execute my judgments against mine enemies, I will cause everyone to be ready, and to prepare their weapons to destroy one another for my Church’s sake.
29:3:13: Thus he shall encourage the enemies when their wickedness is full ripe, to destroy one another, which he calleth the valley of God’s judgment.
29:3:16: God assureth his against all trouble, that when he destroyeth his enemies, his children shall be delivered.
29:3:17: The strangers shall no more destroy his Church: which if they do, it is the people, which by their sins make the breach for the enemy.
29:3:18: He promiseth to his Church abundance of graces, read Ezek. 47:1, which should water and comfort the most barren places, Amos 9:13.
29:3:19: The malicious enemies shall have no part of his graces.
29:3:21: He had suffered his Church hitherto to lie in their filthiness, but now he promiseth to cleanse them and to make them pure unto him.
